# hrc-runtime — Active Invariants

## hrc-runtime.acp-event-bridge

An enabled HRC event bridge observes only committed, allowlisted reason-coded facts and emits the frozen schema-v1 ACP envelope with node-qualified event identity, recorded initiating origin and causation, and a pointer-only payload. Producer emission is durably rate-bounded, runs after commit without affecting the originating write, and is best-effort rather than a second source of truth. V1 activation is disabled by default and confined to the HRC node co-resident with the ACP listener; payload node identity is provenance and a fail-loud tripwire, not execution-routing authority.

## hrc-runtime.architecture-law

Durable HRC architecture laws are stored as machine-checked records with explicit authority, source evidence, required tests, and reopen triggers.

## hrc-runtime.asp-toolchain-selection

Except for the configured aspd-prepared route below, every HRC-owned ASP child spawn resolves its binary at spawn time through one selection authority. A non-empty per-binary command override wins, then the binary's canonical name under an explicitly configured absolute HRC_ASP_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, then the HRC release's resolveHoistedBinary result. No such spawn path, including the legacy interactive stdio broker path, independently selects or caches a command; injected constant commands are test seams only. With HRC_ASPD_SOCKET configured, the aspd-prepared route is HRC-hosted headless codex-app-server whose effective operator presentation is none (explicit request or node default) or whose presentation is tmux-tui selected by an explicit per-request presentation.operator tmux-tui; a node-default tmux-tui with no request choice is not on that route and keeps this resolver. On the aspd-prepared route, for either presentation, HRC spawns no ASP compiler child and launches the worker only from the executionRelease executable and argv prefix committed under hrc-runtime.aspd-prepared-execution-release, and a tmux-tui viewer renderer is launched by that worker from its own release payload, never selected by HRC. That route never consults a per-binary override, HRC_ASP_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, resolveHoistedBinary, PATH, a moving current link, or source for the worker or its renderer, and it has no fallback to them. A configured-root selection that is missing or not executable fails before spawn, and incompatible facade, aspd, or broker protocol/capability hellos fail closed before invocation work. Admin status derives effective source and path for resolver-governed routes from that resolver, keeps the aspd service projection distinct, and distinguishes both from the immutable bundled ASP tuple governed by hrc-runtime.observable-release. The root is one configuration namespace, not an atomic build-identity boundary, and the daemon's in-process ASP imports remain pinned to its release.

## hrc-runtime.bounded-lifecycle-event-observation

HRC owns the lifecycle ledger incarnation and canonical event envelope. Its bounded tail returns the selected ascending page, global head, and incarnation from one transaction. An exclusive-before reverse page requires its expected incarnation, rejects replacement with cursor_invalid and no events, applies exact host-session and generation filters before its descending limit-plus-one read, and reverses only the admitted page to chronological order. Existing head callers that omit the reverse cursor retain their behavior. Its bounded follow stream requires an expected incarnation plus exclusive sequence, atomically admits and pins that ledger incarnation, admits no replacement-ledger event, and orders advisory ready, explicit gap, and canonical event records. Replay, seam, and live admission remain within fixed row and serialized-byte ceilings and are pulled through a one-record transport handoff. Ready is not resumable progress; only a fully received event or gap advances a consumer cursor. This observation contract is distinct from and does not amend hrc-runtime.acp-event-bridge.

## hrc-runtime.bounded-state-retention-writes

A fresh HRC database selects incremental auto-vacuum before journal setup or migration DDL. An existing database whose effective auto-vacuum mode is not incremental remains fail-closed for retention deletes until a coordinated offline full VACUUM installs the pointer map. Each retention batch completes full-predicate candidate discovery as a read before any write begins. The subsequent DELETE receives no more than the adaptive batch size of selected integer primary keys through one bounded JSON set, searches target rows by primary key, and re-evaluates the complete eligibility and terminal/live safety predicate inside the write transaction. Discovery may traverse an arbitrarily large eligible range without writer authority; target-table scan work under the writer is forbidden and bounded-key virtual-table scan work is permitted. The deadline is checked again between discovery and deletion, and concurrent state changes may reduce the deleted count without widening the writer's candidate universe.

## hrc-runtime.canonical-package-publication

Every canonical HRC package set is produced from one clean commit contained by a freshly fetched named canonical ref, carries the exact normative praesidiumBuild tuple, refuses same-name/version replacement, and is verified by cache-empty registry tarball reads before publication succeeds.

## hrc-runtime.collaboration-presentation-authority

HRC presents envelopes, writes presentation receipts and failure dispositions as agent:hrc, and never authors an envelope as an agent principal. An envelope becomes presented only on a LANDING FACT observed on the committed broker stream — submission.absorbed or submission.executed for a submission, the first turn.started of the launch-produced runtime for a launch-carried body — never on admission. A receipt names the runtime and generation the body landed in and an opaque presentation id; no run or turn identity participates in presentation, discharge, or disposal. Turn completion discharges no obligation. Discharge is only an explicit reply, a defer, an operator ack, consumed_by_wait, fyi_presented, or an HRC failure disposition. Disposal is keyed by runtime and ledger sequence: the reminder and failed:ignored follow turn terminals observed for the presented runtime, run or no run, and failed:runtime_terminated follows that runtime's termination. A submission permits body retry only on correlated positive evidence that it was not written or that this exact input was removed. Broker queue withdrawal or expiry qualifies only before driver application; native recall qualifies only when it proves removal of this exact input. Rejection reasons, acceptance, missing identity, RPC failure, post-write cancellation or loss, runtime termination, teardown and TTL do not prove that. Possible-write ambiguity retains the durable intent without body reinjection, presentation, or nonlanding strikes. A possibly_written input.rejected is diagnostic and remains eligible for later consumption evidence; absent deliveryEvidence conveys uncertainty. Proven no-write refusals retain bounded backoff and undeliverable policy. A safely retryable refused STEER re-delivers by refusal CLASS, read from the broker's own admission layer: a capability-layer refusal is a fact about the driver and the next delivery takes the enqueue door, while a state-, policy-, authority- or execution-layer refusal is a fact about the instant and the next delivery retries the steer door after a bounded backoff. HRC never treats a transient refusal as a capability verdict. Delivery intent is durable in HRC's store before any submission is made, one envelope per submission, correlated by origin.envelopeId, and reconciled against committed broker evidence at daemon start, at runtime termination, and periodically; an envelope with an open intent is never actionable. A launch-carried presentation lands on the first turn start of the runtime the launch produced and is recorded as launch_carried. Missing submission identity is recoverable only from one distinct committed admission matching the intent's exact runtime, invocation, origin.envelopeId and broker sequence lower bound captured before dispatch. Zero or multiple candidates, an unproven legacy cursor, or an unconfirmed invocation change remains uncertain; a known submission is never rebound. The canonical HRC cursor cannot bound provenance-only admission events. Retry evidence is durably recorded before releasing the old fence; delayed earlier admissions cannot identify a later attempt. An unidentifiable launch retains uncertainty and cannot authorize another birth to settle it. Local landing bookkeeping precedes the wrkq receipt and retries that receipt under the same pre-minted presentationId/driveAttemptId after transport failure or a crash. Local-only presentation does not establish reminder, D3 disposal, or runtime-lapse eligibility: those require committed receipt success. Successful receipt completion clears its intent, preserving legitimate pointer and reminder delivery. A lost landing fact after possible application now retains uncertainty rather than exercising the former HRC loss/TTL redelivery permission; this does not amend wrkq's own accepted-risk record. Independent envelope terminality retains unresolved delivery as an inspectable terminal hold, excluded from routine wake and periodic candidate sets while correlated late evidence still updates it. Late landing sends no new receipt and never reopens the envelope. A local-only presentation refused by wrong_state is disposed terminal_before_receipt without inventing a presented obligation. FYI receipt terminality is its own idempotent completion, not revocation. Terminal cleanup uses the existing broker withdrawal selector once, recording request intent and outcome. Exact queue removal before application proves removal; aggregate envelope-selector success, not_held, unknown, unavailable and RPC failure do not prove this attempt was removed. Broker-held withdrawal does not clear already injected native text. Launch has no submission to withdraw, and cleanup uncertainty never authorizes native clearing, destructive retry or runtime teardown. Aging may expose uncertainty once, never erase it. One run has one canonical turn-response projection, produced by the shared projectSemanticTurnResponse/finalizeSemanticTurnResponse path. For one run the projection reads turn.message rows in hrc_seq order, drops text-empty rows, and selects the last remaining row marked final=true, or the last remaining row when no row is flagged. It consults the raw runtime buffer only when no non-empty turn.message row exists, then falls back to the run error message, and preserves TURN_TEXT_LIMIT truncation and its marker. Runtime buffers remain raw transport evidence, not canonical response state when a semantic message exists. Response finalization, dispatcher finalOutput and transcript indexing consume this one projection without reimplementing it. That body is evidence about what a turn said and is never a reply, an obligation disposition, or reply-body authority. hrcmail_* rows remain local delivery-intent, presentation, reminder, failure-notice and recovery bookkeeping; they are not room, envelope, obligation, discharge, or reply-body authority.

## hrc-runtime.collaboration-state-retention

messages, collective_history_messages, collective_history_observations, collective_history_replications, and every hrcmail_* table are keep-forever durable collaboration state with no standing TTL or scheduled deletion path. messages is the canonical local message and dedupe ledger and the startup source for collective-history observation. Collective-history message and observation rows preserve authority and provenance, while delivered replication rows are the durable checkpoint that prevents full replay on every restart. hrcmail_* rows preserve local execution, presentation, reminder, failure-notice, idempotency, and recovery state around the wrkq-owned collaboration ledger; they do not become room, envelope, obligation, discharge, or reply-body authority. No TTL or delete path for these classes is introduced without separately approved terminality and replay-fence authority. Keep-forever bars a standing TTL, an age predicate, and any scheduled deletion path; it does not preserve the bookkeeping of a mechanism that has been retired by principal ruling. Retiring one removes its own tables and columns in an explicit forward migration, so that the mechanism's absence is checkable by schema rather than by reading code. Such a migration may only drop rows that were never collaboration state: presentation receipts, reminders, failure notices and the local execution history around them are not eligible.

## hrc-runtime.continuation-history-resume

A non-empty provider continuation key recorded on an HRC session or runtime is durable history: clear, drop, and end operations retain it while recording ordinary fresh-start intent separately as persisted session state. Ordinary run, start, and dispatch recreation suppress automatic continuation reuse while that state is disabled; a later committed continuation.updated enables reuse for its newly recorded key. Explicit hrc resume is status- and clear/drop/terminate-barrier-neutral: it selects the newest recorded key for the normalized target, or the key on a valid pinned session, and fails only when no such key exists or a live-runtime conflict prevents safe reuse. Under the scope-and-lane mint lock, its successor boundary returns a session carrying exactly the selected key with reuse enabled or fails without mutation; a keyless inactive current successor may be bound atomically, a same-key inactive successor may be reused idempotently, and a live or different-key successor conflicts. The read-only session resolve surface exposes retained continuation history independently of automatic-reuse state. Startup repair restores only NULL historical session and runtime keys from each owner's latest non-empty durable broker continuation.updated event, never overwrites a current key, preserves ordinary fresh-start disposition, is idempotent, and completes before request service begins.

## hrc-runtime.harness-broker-admission-client

HRC owns cross-seat scheduling, caller policy, and principal authority while the harness-broker owns per-seat admission mechanism. All HRC broker traffic flows through exactly four class-specific submit methods, one each for steer, queue, exclusive, and preempt; the concrete method names are not law. Admission class is explicit in the method signature and is never selected by a whenBusy parameter; composite behavior such as steer-else-queue is caller composition of typed outcomes. Steer exposes no wait, obligation, or own-response option and resolves only through truthful absorbed or executed disposition. Every obligation-bearing call uses enqueue, invoke, or preempt; blocking callers correlate by submission disposition and then the identified turn terminal rather than by delivery inference. An indeterminate submission.lost is a terminal failed disposition: HRC settles its run immediately, then the following non-retryable invocation.failed marks the runtime crashed and closes the broker client. A failed invocation receives no later input, and the next submission provisions a fresh runtime through HRC's existing cross-seat authority. A summons that births a launch-primed seat rides the launch turn: its landing fact is the born runtime's first turn start, and its presentation receipt carries no invocation input id (the T-07693 class). An interactive launch-carried invoke holds a separate invoke-only rendezvous through its owning run's terminal; the every-door birth singleflight still releases at bare boot, so enqueue, steer, preempt, kicker, and mail admission retain their existing behavior. A warm invoke whose frozen broker capabilities omit exclusive is submitted through the queue class while retaining invoke as its visible HRC door; the admitted class is recorded separately and the caller's completion wait is unchanged. A driver that advertises exclusive retains the direct invoke path. A crossing invoke is registered before it waits and remains protected first by that process-local registration and then by its durable active run row. The agent-loop broker adapter holds the returned owner run id above its replaceable transport client and carries it explicitly through ordinary stop and dispose. An owner-scoped interrupt acts only on that exact active run. An owner-scoped terminate preserves the runtime while another crossing registration or durable active run exists; otherwise it makes the broker invocation non-input-dispatchable synchronously before asynchronous teardown. Omitting owner identity preserves explicit operator lifecycle semantics. Preempt requires operator authority or the sender's authority over the envelope driving the active turn, and never arises from a silent class upgrade. HRC consumes broker capability, seat probe, queue, disposition, manifest, and decision-ledger surfaces without reading harness internals or moving per-seat mechanism into the runtime layer. The wrkq mail kicker reads busy state only from the broker-observed seat turn, never from an HRC run row. An unattributed observed turn is a non-idle turn-observed seat; mail remains HRC-held until ownership is attributed. The kicker delivers a queue-intent envelope to a turn-active seat whose driver advertises the steer class through the STEER door; a turn-active seat without steer receives it through enqueue; an idle seat receives it through enqueue and an absent seat through a launch-carried invoke. Every door carries ONE ENVELOPE PER SUBMISSION with origin.envelopeId as the correlation, and steer-else-queue is kicker composition of typed outcomes and landing evidence, never a whenBusy parameter. A mail hint is a count-only PostToolUse context injection about the seat's outstanding ENQUEUE submissions; it is not a presentation, creates no receipt, submission or obligation, and carries a count and no sender attribution. On a steer-capable seat that count is zero by construction. Each hold/preempt request remains an immediate isolated admission decision.

## hrc-runtime.harness-broker-committed-observation-control

HRC observes and projects only committed normalized harness-broker envelopes, and BrokerEventMapper remains their sole interpreter. For each broker sequence, one SQLite transaction idempotently mirrors the normalized envelope, projects runtime run buffer continuation surface and permission state, appends canonical hrc_events, and advances a contiguous projection cursor or records a typed fenced disposition. The cursor advances across intentionally non-mirrored high-volume deltas without treating mirror retention as a source gap. An execution naming a native turn resolves ownership from immutable broker event evidence keyed by runtime, historical operation generation, invocation, native turn id, and harness generation or turn attempt where present. Event, invocation, operation, and candidate run identities must agree; the current runtime generation is not historical authority. Initiating evidence is an explicit start input, definitive own attribution, or executed submission mapped to its run. A stored start run_id alone, absorbed input, acceptance order, current active run, and newest bracket cannot establish ownership. The controller-persisted launch-carried invoke marker is the narrow legacy exception for that invocation's first input-less launch turn only; it is not native consumption proof. Foreign turns remain unowned. Unknown, absent, or conflicting evidence remains unresolved; the first definitive own attribution may bind an unresolved turn once. Later execution events retain the exact owner even after another turn starts. A named unresolved turn never falls through to submission or bracket inference. Existing no-bracket compatibility remains limited to events without turn identity and without an observed bracket. Immutable attribution events govern; broker_turn_attributions cannot be a competing authority. Attribution sequence bounds prevent future evidence from rewriting an earlier projected row; historical ledger rows are not rewritten. Submission-record resolution is distinct from execution ownership. A definitively absorbed, submission-linked, admission-class steer auxiliary in the same historical epoch with no startedAt settles idempotently against its exact owner, never against itself. Accepted or legacy ACK-completed auxiliaries become terminal coalesced with an owner link, preserved or settlement completion time, no invented start or batch position, and no synthetic execution lifecycle. Failed, cancelled, or zombie auxiliaries retain their truthful status and error when gaining a definitive owner link; a different existing owner conflicts. New steer acknowledgements do not complete auxiliary runs. Delayed definitive ownership settles earlier absorption for that exact turn. Definitive teardown explicitly disposes absorbed auxiliaries whose owner remains unresolved. Neither ordinary nor ledger-inclusive runtime prune may remove the evidence while a definitive absorbed dependency lacks an owner association or explicit unresolved-owner teardown disposition; terminal status alone is insufficient. An old owner's terminal closes only that owner and clears activeRunId only when equal. It cannot fail, finalize, clear, or release a newer execution, mark its invocation ready, or drain its queue through mismatch repair. Only after that transaction commits may HRC acknowledge the broker sequence, notify followers, or evaluate a control policy that depends on the fact. HRC is the sole broker-ledger retention-bearing consumer: its fenced control connection owns one durable scalar acknowledgement per invocation, bounded by forensic and active-invocation holds; read-only observer clients have no acknowledgement identity or retention claim and fail typed below the retained floor. This does not change the keep-forever HRC projection law in hrc-runtime.ledger-tool-result-storage. Control attempts remain typed durable intent over the existing specialized stores, and RPC acceptance never proves provider effect; effects return as later committed observations. The wrkq kicker acts only when committed terminal execution truth and authoritative pending-obligation truth agree, no newer input or turn supersedes them, and the one-reminder bound permits the attempt. Explicit policy operator and API permission decisions are HRC-owned and persist before permission.respond on the fenced control connection. A deadline fallback is broker-owned; HRC later projects its already committed permission.resolved timeout fact.

## hrc-runtime.ledger-tool-result-storage

Outside an explicit include-ledgers runtime cascade, broker_invocation_events and hrc_events rows and their tool-result bytes remain keep-forever. HRC removes duplicate envelope payloads and stores every tool result whose serialized value exceeds 32768 UTF-8 bytes once in tool_result_blobs inside state.sqlite, in the same transaction as deterministic excerpt stubs in the ledger rows. Ordinary reads and live notifications hydrate those stubs; only the dedicated federation read paths expose persisted stubs. Federation schedules the local-blob feed before the ledger feeds and transfers blobs using globally unique deterministic identifiers and addressed, idempotently staged parts no larger than 256 KiB; imported blobs are not re-forwarded. A missing or incomplete blob remains observable as its excerpt and increments ledger.blob_miss rather than making its ledger row unreadable. The current authority is the SQLite blob table, without a filesystem carrier, content hash, feature flag, or standing ledger TTL.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-exact-scope-provisioning

Mobile exact-scope provisioning is one implicit reject-on-occupied START with no inbound host session id and a required durable idempotency key. Registry binding remains authoritative for an established scope. For a virgin scope, origin and receiver derive one home in this order: exact pin, exact home, reserved-family home, explicit typed provision.node directive, profile provisioning default, platform default. For an IMPLICIT mail-kicker birth only, when every preceding placement input is silent and the target remains virgin, the registry host may replace the local platform default with one persisted tier-5 birth designation. It derives that designation itself from wrkq's globally earliest reply-required envelope for the target and one registry consult of that envelope's scoped sender: a bound sender contributes its binding home and a retired sender its immutable retired home. The first designation is recorded before response and every later ask returns it unchanged. Only its home may establish with sender-derived provenance; non-homing kickers finish without starting. Every higher-precedence establishment remains admissible and atomically supersedes a live designation. No designation is recorded for no birth envelope or an absent or unbound sender, and inability to consult wrkq or the registry is a typed retryable refusal with no local fallback. A declared roster base reserves its closed suffix namespace on that home, and profile validation rejects pins or homes for reserved members. An explicit node directive is admissible only when no placement declaration applies and is validated at both origin and receiver against the federation registry and the receiver's own profile; conflicts are typed refusals before mutation. No placement is inferred from ambient caller identity, transport, connection, or environment; the mail default is derived only by the registry host from the authoritative ledger envelope and registry state. A remote home is invoked only through the authenticated, capability-advertised exactStart peer verb, whose receiver independently validates retirement, authority, binding, placement, and materialization capability before mutation and localizes runtime intent. On the authoritative home, exact and suffix claim/start share the same roster:<agentId>:<projectId> mutex and FREE predicate, so canonical exact names overlapping suffix members cannot claim one continuity concurrently. A new exact key either atomically rotates or mints a fresh successor and records its canonical request hash, or returns session_scope_occupied without mutation. Callers omitting materialization retain claim-and-start. The closed first_turn materialization token is part of the request hash; its localized intent, successor, continuity, and claim row commit as one fact for both mint and recycle, and the current awaiting-first-turn successor is occupied until its first real broker-dispatch input materializes the runtime. Creation returns awaiting_first_turn with a nullable runtime id rather than sending an empty turn. Replay validates the request hash and follows the active same-scope/lane prior-host-session chain back to the recorded successor only while every traversed generation has no claim row or the same idempotency key. A claim row under any other key proves supersession, including on an archived intermediate generation. Thus stale rotations preserve ownership, independently claimed descendants never alias, conflicting replays fail before intent mutation, and superseded claims never start archived predecessors. New federation callers forward and parse the nullable-runtime response; an old authoritative peer refuses the unknown materialization field before mutation, while old callers retain started responses. Retryable peer failure is synchronous runtime_unavailable and does not use the message outbox.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-session-index

HRC is the authoritative producer of the Mobile session index: it maintains one current-generation projection per local session lineage; defines recency as the greatest observed contributing activity timestamp; derives effective status and execution mode before reads; and exposes bounded page and facet APIs. Complete federated pages follow the strict order last_activity_at DESC, nodeId ASC, host_session_id DESC through one opaque cursor whose per-node components advance only past emitted rows. Concurrent activity may move a row only toward the head, so a walk has no duplicates or permanent loss; peer failures freeze that peer's component and surface complete:false rather than claiming a complete global interleave. ACP and iOS consume these projections and facets as authoritative and do not acquire peer-probe authority.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-suffix-roster-provisioning

Mobile suffix-roster families are finite. Every enabled ACP quick-pick base has a concrete declared home before the surface is enabled. A declared base reserves every member produced by HRC's fixed ordered suffix list on that home, and profile validation rejects pins or homes for reserved members. An undeclared family may instead use an explicit typed provision.node directive; it is validated at both origin and receiver against the federation registry and the receiver's own profile, and any placement conflict is a typed refusal before mutation. No placement is inferred from caller identity, transport, connection, or environment. Origin HRC routes the whole family from registry binding state and the baseSessionRef-derived family home. A remote home is invoked only through the authenticated, capability-advertised rosterStart peer verb. The receiver independently preflights retirement, authority, binding state, placement, and materialization capability for the whole family before mutation, localizes the runtime intent, and then owns the roster claim and durable idempotency record. Callers omitting materialization retain claim-and-start. For the closed first_turn mode, the localized intent, successor, continuity, and claim row commit atomically for mint and recycle; the awaiting successor is not a free roster slot, creation returns awaiting_first_turn with a nullable runtime id, and the first real broker input materializes it without an empty turn. Replay validates the request hash and audits every generation from active continuity back to the recorded successor through the successor-host claim index. Missing rows inherit ownership through ordinary rotation, the same key is consistent, and any different key on an active or archived intermediate generation returns roster_claim_superseded. New peers forward and parse this shape; old homes reject the unknown field before mutation and old callers retain started responses. Operator starts without an explicit node directive remain explicit-local. Retryable peer failure is synchronous runtime_unavailable and does not use the message outbox.

## hrc-runtime.observable-release

Every atomic HRC release records its exact HRC build and locked ASP build in praesidium-release.json before cutover; the daemon captures that immutable identity at startup, fails closed for invalid atomic manifests, and reports on every status read whether the running release still equals the installed release. Source and worktree daemons report unmanaged explicitly.

## hrc-runtime.participant-session-lifecycle

HRC owns protocol registration, addresses, sessions, attempt identity and activation. A participant's own registration message creates an available address without ASP admit, adapter availability, or descriptor/evidence-file prerequisites. Direct registration requires no configured class. Missing class, adapter, workspace and preparation are represented as NULL, never invented; existing keyed registration identities survive migration. Resolved ownership and address policy are durable independently of adapter lookup. Registry-first local registration returns a durable address before driver attachment. A wrong node returns the canonical home for caller retry, with no local allocation or new forwarding protocol. HRC reserves runtime identity before attachment but materializes the runtime row only after real profile and broker facts exist. An unprepared IDENTITY_MINTED attempt is non-runnable, consumes no establishment retries and survives daemon loss. Attachment atomically freezes validated profile and environment, transitions to PREPARED and arms existing durable work; duplicate attachment does not reset a running or exhausted retry budget. Replacement-intent work remains independently discoverable. ASP preparation is optional post-join driver configuration, not authority to register. It returns only the existing execution profile and optional dispatch environment, never HRC runtime handles or lifecycle policy. Existing profile structure, identity and hash checks apply at attachment without new security requirements. Broker ownership must agree with the resolved join direction; external process ownership is the direct default, and managed ownership requires HRC's committed launch record and host-aware guard, never a class name alone. Three boundaries remain distinct: freeze the validated ASP result before hosting; persist HRC hosting intent including its selected lifecycle policy before realization, then persist actual or rediscovered leases; finally compose and atomically persist the complete dispatch before scheduling the first ensure. HRC alone constructs runtime overlays from actual leases and composes resource environment values under existing environment ownership and locked-env checks. The broker pane is never an operator presentation pane. Ensure retries use the exact frozen tuple; policy reload or missing resources cannot edit it under the same start attempt. Participant-served join spawns no broker through HRC; any required HRC presentation resource is independently realized or refused without fabricating ownership. A controlled ASP adapter proves both joins through the installed Phase 2 path; native Phase 3 and direct-lowering proofs remain separate. Hosted and participant-served brokers share the registration lifecycle with declared address and continuity policies. Host lifecycle ownership is a declared class policy, never inferred from broker join; HRC hosting a broker conveys only broker resource ownership. Under continuity key-scoped, a permanent key retains its scope, host session, and generation across native host restart and observer replacement. Under continuity host-incarnation, one selected address binds at most one live host incarnation and one host incarnation binds at most one address, enforced by durable constraints. A selected address is established in the collective binding registry through the existing registry-first summon-authority path before any local reservation, session, or binding exists; resolving a home is insufficient, and a refused, unreachable, bound-elsewhere, or designation-mismatched establishment writes nothing locally. An address reservation is independent of any incarnation, is not free in any runtime or binding state, transfers rather than releases at succession, survives operator eviction, and is freed only by explicit attributed release. Mail to an absent bound host remains pending and never births a substitute. processToken is opaque compatibility input ignored for joining, not persisted HRC identity, an HRC comparison key, or replacement authority. Registration remains durable when observation is unavailable. Each durable attempt has one invocation identity. Identity installation, hello, resident invocation establishment, attach confirmation, and activation are distinct. HRC persists the immutable start request and dispatch options before requesting resident establishment. Broker-owned durable start receipts serialize matching retries, refuse conflicting reuse, and record starting before driver side effects. Lost replies never repeat driver.start; uncertain restart or a started receipt without its resident invocation remains indeterminate until broker or adapter evidence reconciles or retires the attempt. Hosted creation persists identity, paths, command, and credential before spawn; serialized rediscovery bypasses credential rewrites and duplicate window creation, and an unverifiable incumbent blocks. Live or pending attempts cannot be superseded by ordinary registration. An epoch is a concurrency precondition, not replacement authority. Successor admission requires an absorbing prior disposition and broker-owned irreversible retirement or verified prior writer death. Retirement closes every path to new native writes before acknowledgement. Retry exhaustion, transport loss, and an empty unresolved-write store do not prove retirement. Unresolved input remains independently broker-fenced across replacement without resend, cancellation, inferred outcome, or manufactured turn failure. Epochs fence control and outbox work, not validated historical evidence. Writer evidence answers only for its declared host or bridge subject; bridge evidence never authorizes host succession, host evidence is not required for bridge replacement, HRC may inspect only a process it launched and owns, and external native evidence remains adapter-owned. Write-path retirement, writer liveness, and prior-event recovery are independent three-valued facts, with unknown holding admission. Evidence-backed retirement or death moves a nonabsorbing displaced attempt to ABANDONED with its reason, including after activation; TERMINAL remains exclusive to projection of a producer-authored terminal. Attempt abandonment never implies recovery abandonment. A same-host bridge replacement preserves scope, session, generation, and runtime, advances attempt, invocation, bridge instance, and attach epoch, and emits no resume; late validated evidence remains attributed to its old invocation and cannot close or mutate the current run, obligation, or continuation. Host succession compares against the observed predecessor. A first transaction commits the evidence-backed prior disposition and moves an old host binding to retiring while preserving pending replacement work and the reservation; the resulting no-successor state is valid and recoverable. After the independent retirement, absorbing-state, and recovery gates pass, a second transaction rechecks the gates and predecessor fences and atomically commits final binding retirement, the successor session and work, reservation transfer, and staged replay fences. Neither allocation transaction rewrites an absorbing attempt, and the address is never observably free. Activation requires the current attempt's confirmed attach and commits its binding classification once. Unknown continuity evidence preserves known evidence and emits no resume; first known evidence attaches, unchanged known evidence replaces, and changed known evidence resumes under the same session. Replay remains durable and unacknowledged until projected; successor replay is released only after activation and prior recovery reconciled or explicitly abandoned with a reason. Recovery projects committed prior-invocation evidence without restoring its control authority, repairing its ledger, or mutating retention acknowledgements. A recovered producer terminal is distinct from broker loss with unknown native outcome. Automatic continuation reuse at host succession respects explicit clear barriers and disabled reuse using HRC's own records, not an adapter verdict. The selected continuation and selection reason are durable and returned to the participant. Attachment must express that selection in the existing continuation field before profile freeze; mismatch cannot silently become a fresh start. A newer clearing barrier is rechecked before freeze. Resume request states not_requested, requested, unsupported and indeterminate are persisted separately from carried history; joining or broker hello never proves native resume success. Unsupported resume preserves history and pending input until explicit disposition. Explicit historical resume is not the automatic selector. External process-fate law follows durable lifecycle ownership, while acknowledgement ownership follows the controlling client. Legacy observers without native lifetime capability remain not-activated and emit no invented resume. A managed host launch persists a unique non-secret launchId before spawn and adopts only the returning registration correlated to that launch record; launchId grants no permission and changes no authentication. Save and exit are separate managed-host readbacks and may each be unknown. Graceful stop refuses or remains indeterminate rather than forcing after failed, refused, missing, or timed out save evidence; forced closure is explicit per call and reports data-loss knowledge truthfully. Managed host lifecycle is refused until every runtime lifecycle reader is host-aware, and absence of the external marker never alone authorizes process disposal, reaping, or termination. Queue and steer remain the federation control contract; interrupt and preempt are not advertised, and internal children mint no HRC seat or satisfy the parent's obligation. EPR grant behavior remains unchanged. Revision 7 is operator-authorized implementation work, not implementation acceptance and does not accept final-tail loss; Phase 5 completeness requires its separately verified retention and catch-up contract without dependence on a future user resume.

## hrc-runtime.quarantined-release-sweep

Phase 1 quarantine remains reversible and keeps every observed reference. Phase 2 may unlink only valid release-id children of the owning user's .gc-quarantine during an operator-scheduled quiescence window, within the hrc-runtime.quarantined-release-sweep-scan-coherence accepted-risk boundary. Before mutation, the daemon is absent and held down, current-code maintenance and install exclusion is held, the release root and quarantine are owner-owned mode 0700, and two complete clean ps plus privileged open-path observations cover the exact candidate set with an unchanged pid-and-start-time incarnation set. Probe status, output completeness, attestation nonce and candidate scope fail closed. Privilege may actuate supervision and read process state, but every unlink runs as the release owner. Each surviving candidate remains bit-for-bit unmodified on refusal. After all safety gates pass, each candidate transition is ordered: reassert daemon absence, write .sweep-in-progress, recursively set every directory in that candidate to mode 0700, then unlink that same candidate. A sentinel-bearing survivor is non-restorable partial-sweep residue completed by a later successful sweep. Elapsed quarantine age is operator convenience, never evidence of reference absence.

## hrc-runtime.transcript-search-projection

HRC transcript search is a resident hrc-server-maintained, rebuildable bounded projection of broker_invocation_events and is never source-of-truth state or a manual freshness step. Its implementation begins as the separate hrc-transcript-index package, with projection tables owned by hrc-store-sqlite and thin operator/query surfaces in the hrc CLI. One document represents one terminated invocation turn: each turn.completed, turn.failed, or turn.interrupted terminal closes the exact invocation-sequence segment since the preceding terminal, no document crosses a terminal, and no terminal-less segment emits a document. Documents carry terminal status and exact runtime, invocation, seq-from, and seq-to identity. Searchable content contains only user-message prose and assistant-message-completed prose, partitions canonical assistant text with the shared last-final-true-else-last-non-empty selector, excludes tool calls, tool results, lifecycle notices, and narration classification, and applies configured per-column byte bounds. The global ledger-id cursor detects relevant events only: every emitted segment is reconstructed from the authoritative ledger in invocation seq order. Each bounded scan captures a ledger-id ceiling, advances the cursor to that ceiling when complete, and can report zero lag at quiescence. Cursor, per-invocation terminal high-water mark, and emitted rows advance atomically; prose or terminals arriving at or below an emitted high-water mark cause that invocation to be reprojected from its ledger terminals. FTS5 content rows and external-content index remain transactionally aligned. Scope, project, agent, task, generation, runtime, invocation, and sequence identity remain plain columns; scope is a facet and runtime_id is the transcript hand-off key. Ranking negates bm25 so larger scores are better, evaluates bm25 and snippets inside the FTS query before windowing, ranks candidates within each runtime, and uses the single strongest turn rather than summing evidence across a scope; per-runtime candidate caps bound discovery monopolization. Every hit renders the exact runtime and sequence-range transcript hand-off. An explicit include-ledgers runtime prune deletes matching transcript documents and per-invocation projection marks in the same transaction as their source ledger rows. Rebuild is an operator recovery surface, not normal operation. The local CLI surface adds neither redaction nor authentication or authorization.

## hrc-runtime.verify-gate

The declared verify gate checks architecture records and their generated projections in addition to build, structural checks, lint, types, tests, and the fixture-owned federation loopback corpus. Enforcement note (T-08054): the pre-push path captures stdin once, runs lock-hygiene first under `piped: true`, replays the refs through the unchanged code-validation gate, and posts `git.push` only at the successful tail; tracked executable `.githooks/post-commit` enters the best-effort `git.commit` producer.

## hrc-runtime.viewer-presentation-sidecar

HRC owns runtime lifecycle and the durable presentation facts needed to reconstruct viewer intent, but after viewer cutover it never actuates Ghostty. Each start or reuse publishes runtime.presentation with the invocation-local operator-attach suppression decision, while the runtime generation persists only operator attachability, latest viewer window, and monotone viewerRequested intent. A store-only presentation read model exposes those facts without probing or mutating runtimes. hrc-viewer alone actuates Ghostty through ghostmux and keeps no persistent registry outside Ghostty pane metadata. Raising or focusing an existing pane by a user-principal tool (a CLI the human runs on their own desktop, e.g. hcs) is not presentation actuation for this invariant: it mints, stamps, rebinds, retitles, and closes nothing, and focus is never read for identity or topology decisions. Such a tool may read the pane metadata the viewer wrote to locate a pane; it may not write it. Exactly one viewer-bearing daemon is permitted per GUI user and it is the production daemon; non-production daemons for that user keep their in-daemon Ghostty viewer disabled and never run hrc-viewer. This placement constraint is the authority boundary for the user's shared Ghostty registry; the design does not provide cross-daemon pane ownership or isolation. Within that one viewer, the single global pane for a logical session is keyed by normalized (scopeRef, laneRef), with runtime and generation fences for adoption and reap. A pre-record generation is adopt-only and cannot cause a pane to be minted until an invocation establishes presentation authority. Viewer absence, death, lag, reconnect, reconciliation, and polling cannot mutate or finalize runtime, run, or turn state and cannot delay or fail their lifecycle paths.
